newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Clinton, Boutros-Ghali shake hands at U.N..
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Boutros-Ghali shake hands at U.N..

text.p: President Bill Clinton exchanged a cordial handshake with Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali -- the man he has vowed to oust -- after arriving at U.N. headquarters on Tuesday to address the General Assembly.
Before his speech, he became the first signatory of an agreement halting all nuclear test explosions.
The handshake took place as Clinton and Boutros-Ghali smiled and posed for photographers in front of U.S. and U.N. flags at the U.N. delegates' entrance.
Neither made any statement before the U.N. chief ushered the president into a nearby office suite behind the Assembly hall.

A U.N. spokesman said much of their conversation, which lasted only about 15 minutes, focused on African issues. They also touched on the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty that Clinton was about to sign and the difficulty of arousing public interest in long-range problems.
But there was no discussion of their differences about who should be secretary-general, the U.N. spokesman said.

Clinton told reporters at the White House on Monday he still opposed a second term for the 73-year-old Egyptian diplomat whose current five-year term as secretary-general expires at the end of the year. The United States has repeatedly said the world organisation needs new leadership to carry out reforms.
"Our position on the future of the U.N. and the secretary-general, a man for whom I have great personal respect, has been clear for many months now. So nothing's changed there," Clinton said.
